title: Anonymous figure cipher, 28 October 1586, BnF Clairambault 357 ff. 167-168 (catalogue item 14)

plaintext.source: f. 168r is a clear copy of f. 167r ll. 1-30; from the ✝ mark to the end the decipherer wrote the plaintext between the lines.

transcription.notes: No ciphertext transcription file was made; only sample runs were decoded against the glosses.

system.summary: Homophonic two-digit figure substitution in a continuous stream with a few nomenclator signs and nulls, dropping into clear in places.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's partial reconstruction (henryiii_Anonymous.png), checked and extended (87 = e, 71 = a, 22 null).
system.notes: 78 vous, 81 que, 83 il, 92 et; signs for Roy de Navarre, Angleterre, Monsieur de Mayne, Navarre.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear copy (f. 168r) and interlinear decipherment bound with the letter; Tomokiyo's partial key online

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Found the Gallica ark via SRU dc.source and fetched ff. 167r, 167v, 168r at full resolution.
Recognised f. 168r as the clear text of f. 167r to the ✝ mark and the interlinear glosses as the decipherment of the rest.
Decoded sample runs with Tomokiyo's key; all agree with the glosses and f. 168; key extended (87 = e, 71 = a).
Transcribed f. 168r and the interlinear glosses as the text of the letter.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryption (f. 168r clear copy + interlinear glosses) and key table copied from NOTES.md to texts/; no full cipher transcription exists, so texts/f167_transcription.txt holds only the sample figure runs from NOTES.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/f167_decryption.md read. The f. 168r clear copy builds sentences; the interlinear part (f. 167r after the cross, f. 167v) is fragments with holes in most sentences. Entry split into a read part and a decoded, not read part; class read -> read in part; fraction_read unknown -> about 0.5 (estimated).

f. 167r from the cross mark and f. 167v transcribed line by line on the full-resolution canvases 331-332: clear text, interlinear glosses and figure groups (texts/f167_interlinear_transcription.txt). Corrects earlier fragments: 'Cambaronne' = l'embarquement, 'Coride' = a la Floride (le feu admiral), 'Saisonne' = vaisseaulx, 'Il se trouvera' = Il se promectoit; recto 'et que luy' runs on into the verso.

Unglossed and cut groups decoded with key.md (research/reading_audit/b26_clair_dec.py): si vous y voulliez entendre, avec moy se negoce a bonne fin, l'embarquement, le feu admiral a la Floride, neantmoings on se servira de ceste occasion a conclure la paix; 73 = d confirmed. Reading texts/f167_interlinear_reading.md scored 0.758 (explicit holes 0.909); sentences hold; relabelled read (grade B).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 2 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent check of the f. 168r clear copy against the cipher it copies. The seven figure lines of f. 167r before the cross (ll. 23-29, 266 figure groups) read on the Gallica image (canvas 331) into texts/f167r_l23-29_figures_dudout.txt and decoded with Tomokiyo's table plus key.md (verify_dudout_20261114.py, not b26_clair_dec.py): 293 of 311 letters agree with the copy; the rest are 9 groups outside the key (30, 33, 46, 48, 75, 79, 89, 90, 94) and two surplus 7s after 27. The decode settles three doubtful passages of f168_reading.md, each re-read on the f. 168r image (canvas 333): 'faisant des stances [?] et autres places' is 'faisant instance des autres places'; 'que vous n'y quictez rien. La poursuite ne les travaux [?] de la brouillerie du Roy de Navarre' is 'que vous ne quictez ny la poursuicte ny l'esperance pour la reconciliation du Roy de Navarre'; 'luy de [protecteur?] ... Catholiques ... Huguenotz ... qui passe avant' is 'l'un de proteger les Catholiques, l'autre les Huguenotz, sans l'autre qui passe avant'. New in the key, read against the copy: 46 = les (3x), the double-barred cross = Catholiques, the barred circle = Huguenotz (confirmed), 94 = t (2x), 89 = ff, 33 = c. f168_reading.md and f168_en.md corrected; v10_relabel share of f168_reading.md 0.955 -> 0.964 (recorded read_share and class left unchanged). See VERIFY_dudout_20261114.md.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his decoder re-run (293 of 311 letters of ll. 23-29 agree with the f. 168r copy; 222 of 235 after the cross). Canvas 331: the last line before the cross and the line beginning 25 28 82 (about 75 groups) agree with his transcription. Canvas 333: the copy reads 'la poursuicte ny l'esperance pour la reconciliation' and 'l'un de proteger les Catholiques ... les Huguenotz sans', as he says; 'ferez congnoistre' (cipher 35 28 43 28 41) adopted in f168_reading.md where he had left 'faire'. NOTES Text, texts/f167_decryption.md and the key section (texts/key.md) brought into line: the three corrected passages, the sample run with 82, 46 = les, 94 = t, 89 = ff, 33 = c, the Catholiques sign, the barred circle = Huguenotz. read_share of the f. 168r entry 0.955 -> 0.964 (v10_relabel.measure, 371 words, 14 holes). Class unchanged. ll. 1-22 of f. 167r remain untranscribed.

outcome.method_basis: The letter is covered by a contemporary clear copy on f. 168r (to the cross mark) and an interlinear decipherment on f. 167r-v after it, both bound with the cipher; Tomokiyo's partial key was used only to check the two layers against the figures.
outcome.notes: Read from the contemporary decipherment, not by decoding every group; several uncertain words and verso names remain open. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the entry split; the f. 168r copy reads, the f. 167 interlinear part is decoded, not read; class read -> read in part. 23 Oct 2026 (b26): the f. 167 interlinear part re-read line by line at full resolution (glosses, clear stretches, unglossed groups decoded): it reads (grade B); both entries read; class read in part -> read.

texts.label: ff. 167-168, 28 Oct 1586: f. 168r, the contemporary clear copy of f. 167r ll. 1-30 (to the cross mark)
texts.summary: A Catholic nobleman of the Angoumois or Saintonge writes on 28 October 1586, probably to Henri, duc de Guise: he has been ill for two months, reports Catherine de Médicis's negotiation with Navarre, says Navarre's Catholic confidant Fumé, vice-admiral of Guyenne, has repeatedly proposed a reconciliation between Navarre and the addressee, and mentions the Queen of England and Villeroy's letter about satisfying Mayenne.

reading_review.note: The f. 168r clear copy builds French sentences with scattered [?] and (…) holes; the last sentence is uncertain.

texts.label: ff. 167-168, 28 Oct 1586: f. 167r from the cross mark and f. 167v, interlinear decipherment and the clear stretches between the cipher lines
texts.summary: The rest of the letter: Fumée, vice-admiral of Guyenne and Navarre's Catholic confidant, has repeatedly proposed a reconciliation with Navarre and would bring it to a good end; by it the war could be opened in England, and Fumée would supply ships for the embarkation under cover of another voyage; the writer compares the plan with Coligny's Florida venture; letters for the Queen of Navarre sent through Randan; Villeroy writes about satisfying Mayenne, the withdrawal of the reiters and Swiss, and a peace with the Huguenots that would ruin the country.

reading_review.note: Contemporary interlinear glosses and the writer's clear text, transcribed line by line at full resolution, unglossed groups decoded with key.md; 0.758 clean sentences (explicit holes 0.909); a few doubtful words (son [?edit], [?des lettres]) and one cut gloss.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 94.2% of the words of texts/f167_interlinear_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
